plain.text: When Isaac was old and almost blind, he told Esau to hunt some game and prepare his favourite meal, so that he could give him his blessing before he died. Rebekah overheard and told Jacob to bring two young goats so she could make the meal, and Jacob could receive the blessing instead. Jacob worried that Esau was hairy and he was smooth. Rebekah put Esau's clothes on Jacob and covered his hands and neck with goatskins. Jacob went in and said, "I am Esau, your firstborn." Isaac was suspicious: "The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau." He asked again, and Jacob lied again. Isaac ate, kissed him and blessed him with plenty, and said nations would serve him and he would be lord over his brothers.

Just after Jacob left, Esau came in with the meal. Isaac trembled violently: someone had already received the blessing, "and indeed he will be blessed". Esau cried out bitterly, "Bless me too, my father!" Isaac said Jacob had taken it by deceit. Esau said, "Isn't he rightly named Jacob? He has deceived me twice: he took my birthright, and now my blessing!" Isaac gave Esau a lesser blessing: he would live by the sword and serve his brother, but one day throw off his yoke. Esau hated Jacob and planned to kill him after Isaac died. Rebekah heard and told Jacob to flee to her brother Laban in Haran until Esau's anger cooled. She told Isaac she could not bear for Jacob to marry a local woman.

summary.bigIdea: Jacob, with his mother's help, deceives his father to steal Esau's blessing, tearing the family apart.
points: Rebekah and Jacob trick blind Isaac.
Jacob receives the blessing; Esau weeps bitterly.
Esau plans to kill Jacob, who must flee.
summary.reflection: Every person in this family hurt the others. Where do you see the harm deceit can cause in families?
